message.content:
To solve \(6n \equiv 7 \pmod{13}\), find the inverse of \(6\) modulo \(13\).

Since
\[
6 \cdot 11 = 66 \equiv 1 \pmod{13},
\]
the inverse of \(6\) modulo \(13\) is \(11\).

Multiply both sides by \(11\):
\[
n \equiv 7 \cdot 11 \equiv 77 \pmod{13}.
\]
Now reduce:
\[
77 - 65 = 12,
\]
so
\[
n \equiv 12 \pmod{13}.
\]

The answer is 12.
